subject: RFI: Adaptive alerting & investigator handoff for content abuse
messages:
From: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@cobaltbank.com>
To: sofia_ivanova, vanessa_ortiz
Cc: secproc@cobaltbank.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Adaptive alerting & investigator handoff for content abuse

Hi Sofia / Vanessa —

Thanks for taking our RFI. As part of our procurement packet we need a focused section on operational handoffs and alert fidelity. Can you confirm the following for Redwood Inference:

1) What adaptive alerting tiers do you support (examples: low/med/high, custom thresholds, anomaly detection) and how are they mapped to human investigator queues?

2) What enrichment fields accompany each alert (e.g., confidence score, policy tags, model id, token span, source input length, streaming vs full-response flag)? Please supply a schema or sample webhook payload.

3) SLA for acknowledgement and first-investigator-assignment for high-severity abuse reports (business hours vs 24/7).

4) How do you preserve chain-of-custody and evidence for audits (redaction options, immutable logs, retention default and configurable windows)?

5) Are there built-in integrations for case management (Jira/ServiceNow) and do you support a case-id handoff with enriched context?

We attached our question list (Cobalt_RFI_questions.pdf). Can you reply with a concise capability summary and any sample schemas by EOD 27 Apr?

Best,
Elena Moreno
Head of Security Operations
Cobalt Bank
[attachment: Cobalt_RFI_questions.pdf (pdf, 210KB)]
From: sofia_ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@cobaltbank.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz, markus_klein, jasmine_liu
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Adaptive alerting & investigator handoff for content abuse

Elena —

Appreciate the clear ask. Summary answers below and I've attached two artifacts: an alert/enrichment schema (.pdf) and a text file with a sample webhook payload. If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min technical walkthrough next week.

1) Adaptive alerting tiers:
- Default tiers: low / medium / high.
- Custom policies: customers can define threshold rules, anomaly detectors (statistical baselines over request vectors), and model-confidence-based escalations.
- Mapping: High -> immediate paging to on-call investigator queue; Medium -> batched investigator digest (near real-time); Low -> aggregated daily review.

2) Enrichment fields (high-level):
- alert_id, case_id (if auto-created), timestamp, model_id, model_version, confidence_score (0-1), matched_policy_tags (list), category_hierarchy (e.g., abuse->fraud->phishing), token_span (start/end), source_channel (api/stream/console), request_metadata (client_id, region), sampling_flag, kv_cache_hit (boolean).
- See attached adaptive_alerting_schema_v2.pdf for field definitions and retention semantics.
- Sample webhook payload attached (sample_webhook_payload.txt). Example includes an event with pre-signed evidence links and a SHA256 hash for artifacts.

3) SLA commitments (proposed for enterprise plans):
- High severity: acknowledgement within 1 hour (24/7), investigator assignment within 4 hours (business-case dependent).
- Medium severity: acknowledgement within 4 hours (business hours), assignment within 24 hours.
- Low severity: batched review, SLA negotiable.
- We can offer tighter SLAs as part of Dedicated/Enterprise contracts and include an escalation path to engineering on-call.

4) Audit & chain-of-custody:
- Immutable audit trail: append-only event log with signed event entries, stored for default 90 days (configurable up to 7 years) and exportable on request.
- Redaction modes: field-level redaction (PII scrub), automatic redaction based on policy rules, and customer-managed encryption keys (KMS/HSM).
- Evidence links are time-limited pre-signed URLs; we additionally store artifact hashes to validate integrity.

5) Case management integrations:
- Native case object that supports an external_case_id field for linking to Jira/ServiceNow.
- Out-of-the-box connectors: Jira Cloud, ServiceNow; webhook-driven integrations for bespoke systems. Case handoff payload includes alert enrichment, top evidence snippets (with redaction metadata), recommended severity, and a suggested triage checklist.

Attachments: adaptive_alerting_schema_v2.pdf, sample_webhook_payload.txt

Let us know if you want us to map this to your internal Cobalt severity definitions; we can produce a short mutual action plan.

Thanks —
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Safety & Trust
Redwood Inference
[attachment: adaptive_alerting_schema_v2.pdf (pdf, 78KB)]
[attachment: sample_webhook_payload.txt (txt, 4KB)]
From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: sofia_ivanova
Cc: vanessa_ortiz, jasmine_liu
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Adaptive alerting & investigator handoff for content abuse

Sofia — quick internal note to align:
- For enterprise SLA wording we should avoid absolute "assignment within X hours" language unless it's in the contract; propose we phrase as "acknowledgement within 1 hour and target investigator assignment within 4 hours for High severity; contractually configurable."
- On evidence retention: default 90 days is fine, but call out that for regulated customers we support 7-year retention with archival export (on-prem export + secure transfer).
- I'll draft the formal SLA paragraph and a short runbook for the technical walkthrough.

Markus
VP, Product Ops
Redwood Inference
From: sofia_ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@cobaltbank.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz, markus_klein, jasmine_liu
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 14:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Adaptive alerting & investigator handoff for content abuse

Elena —

Thanks for the patience. Per your EOD target, attached is a concise capability summary and two artifacts (schema + webhook sample). Highlights and clarifications: 

- SLA language: we propose to include a contract table with acknowledgement and assignment targets; final wording will be in the Dedicated/Enterprise contract. We will provide a service credit framework for SLA misses.

- Investigator handoff: Cases created by Redwood include an external_case_id and an events array. The webhook includes evidence_links (pre-signed), evidence_hashes, and a triage_recommendation field. You can configure whether evidence links include raw request payload or redacted snippets.

- Enrichment & telemetry: all alerts include model.performance.metrics (latency percentile, token_count) to help triage model-related vs input-related issues. We also attach a sampling_id for customers to correlate with internal logging.

- Security controls: support for customer-supplied KMS keys for artifact encryption, SOC 2 Type II attestation (can provide report under NDA), and SAML SSO for investigator console access.

Next steps: 1) Confirm if Cobalt wants the walkthrough (30 min technical) — propose Wed 5/5 or Thu 5/6; 2) If you want, we will provide a redlined SLA paragraph and a short MOP (runbook) ahead of that call.

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/4891), Drive folder for artifacts (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Axy-example)

Sofia
Director, Safety & Trust
Redwood Inference
